principle.caption: The principle
principle.title: The layer a rapid test does not cover
principle.lead: The six analyses complement point-of-care testing on the Igloo reader with what it does not show: individual predisposition and regulatory processes that change over time.

cards.title: Two layers: genetics and epigenetics
cards.text: Genetic variants describe unchangeable predisposition. Epigenetic markers — microRNA and DNA methylation — show the regulatory state: they follow lifestyle and can be measured over time.

cards.title: Sample material: dried blood card
cards.text: A few drops of capillary blood from the fingertip go onto a dried blood card. No venipuncture, no centrifuge, no cold chain — sampling in the practice or at home.

cards.title: Laboratory and reference data

analyses.caption: Portfolio
analyses.title: The six analyses
analyses.lead: Every analysis runs through the same sampling route. What differs is scope, method and the question it answers.

items.name: Metabolic Health
items.subtitle: Diet by predisposition — epigenetically verifiable.
items.what: The analysis evaluates which distribution of macronutrients suits the individual predisposition, supported by specific portion and recipe suggestions. Because genetic variants do not explain weight behaviour on their own, epigenetic markers of DNA stability and inflammation are assessed in addition: only those respond to lifestyle and work as a measure of success.
who: Where previous dietary changes have not worked

items.name: Healthy Aging
items.subtitle: Biological age across four layers — traffic light, not one number.
items.what: Telomere length, epigenetic ageing markers, inflammation and DNA stability are placed against age- and sex-related reference values and each rated green, amber or red. This shows which layer is driving the result — and where an intervention should start. Lifestyle data is recorded alongside and contrasted with the molecular findings.
who: People aged roughly 40 and over tracking the trend

items.name: Biological age clock
items.subtitle: An exploratory lifestyle signal — not an age determination.
items.what: Three microRNAs are determined by quantitative PCR, normalised against miR-93 and combined into a single value: the percentage deviation of biological from chronological age. The underlying model is published but declared a pilot study — the output is an exploratory signal, not a robust biological age.
who: Health centres, coaching and workplace health
Where a full ageing panel would be too extensive

items.name: Telomere Analysis
items.subtitle: The protective caps of the chromosomes — measured in kilobase pairs.
items.what: Telomeres shorten with each cell division and are regarded as a marker of cellular ageing. Measurement is performed from dried capillary blood, reported in kilobase pairs and placed against an age- and sex-matched reference population. qPCR values vary considerably between runs and laboratories — the trend carries the message, not the single value.
who: Workplace programmes with a longevity focus

items.name: Stress Monitor
items.subtitle: Measured alongside perceived strain — four areas.
items.what: Physiological strain, cell protection, serotonin regulation and immune signals are each reported as a traffic light and contrasted with the subjective stress experience recorded in a questionnaire. The discrepancy is what makes the conversation useful: people with high tolerance for strain frequently underestimate their own load.

items.name: Healthy Sport
items.subtitle: Eight microRNAs in seven assessments; Plus variant adds four variants.
items.what: Nutrient status, hydration status, load and stress level, injury risk and recovery, cardiovascular fitness, inflammation and muscle status — seven assessments from eight microRNAs — form the variable monitoring part. The Plus variant adds four unchangeable genetic variants on sport type, training motivation, muscle damage risk and weight regulation — recorded once.

evidence.caption: Evidence base
evidence.title: What is established — and what is not
evidence.lead: This field is heavily over-promised. Anyone presenting these analyses should know the limits — with professionals, candour is an advantage, not a risk.

established.title: Lifestyle changes epigenetic markers
established.text: Randomised pilot trial over 8 weeks: epigenetic age on average 3.2 years lower than in the control group (Fitzgerald et al., Aging 2021) — DNA methylation, not microRNA.

established.title: Inflammation as an ageing axis
established.text: "Inflammaging" is an established concept; miR-21 is described as a circulating inflammation marker (Olivieri et al. 2012).

established.title: microRNAs are stable in dried blood
established.text: microRNAs are considered more robust than mRNA and remain comparatively stable in dried samples — the sampling route itself is sound.

established.title: The established standard for biological age
established.text: That is methylation clocks: Horvath, PhenoAge, GrimAge and DunedinPACE. DunedinPACE shows high test-retest reliability and associations with morbidity and mortality.

preliminary.title: microRNA age clock
preliminary.text: The published model (n = 539) explains about 5 % of the variance in age, mean absolute error 10.4 years; two of the three markers did not correlate significantly with chronological age.

preliminary.title: Telomere length by qPCR
preliminary.text: The method varies between runs and laboratories; DNA extraction, storage and cell composition all contribute. From dried blood more than from venous blood.

preliminary.title: Gene-based dietary advice
preliminary.text: The Food4Me study found no difference in weight loss between levels of personalisation including genetics. The benefit lies in structure, conversation and adherence.

preliminary.title: microRNA as stress markers
preliminary.text: There is work on individual microRNAs and acute as well as chronic stress, but no established cut-offs and no diagnostic validation.

items.q: What is the difference between genetics and epigenetics?
items.a: Genetic variants are unchangeable for life and are recorded once; epigenetic markers describe the current regulatory state and can be measured over time. Only the epigenetic layer works as a measure of success — set out in full under “Understanding the values”.

A few drops of capillary blood from the fingertip go onto a dried blood card and dry there. No venipuncture, no centrifuge, no cold chain — sampling is possible in the practice or at home. The card is sent to the partner laboratory in the prepared envelope.

items.q: When does a follow-up measurement make sense?
items.a: After 4 to 6 months at the earliest and under conditions as similar as possible. The trend carries the message, not the single value — an initial and a follow-up measurement together form a plannable programme. Acute infections shift inflammation markers, so the timing should be chosen deliberately.

items.q: Do these analyses replace clinical diagnostics?
items.a: No. They are consultation and monitoring tools, not a medical diagnosis and not a substitute for clinical assessment. Where findings suggest a condition requiring treatment, the person belongs in medical or psychotherapeutic assessment.

In Germany, genetic analyses are subject to the Genetic Diagnostics Act: the person examined must be informed and give written consent before sampling, and this must be documented. It applies to Metabolic Health and to the Plus variant of Healthy Sport.

That differs by analysis, and we state it openly. The sampling route itself is sound, as is the monitoring approach. The microRNA age clock, by contrast, is exploratory, and qPCR telomere values vary considerably. The evidence sheet separates established from preliminary evidence and names the sources.
B2B terms on request, tiered by volume and contract model. There is no public consumer price list. Test cards, shipping material and report delivery are part of the offer.

items.q: Which organisations is the programme suitable for?
items.a: The analyses are supplied to professional users only: prevention and longevity practices, nutritional counselling, sports medicine and coaching, and workplace health management.

basics.caption: Understanding the values
basics.title: What the reports actually measure
basics.lead: The reports contain values from four levels. Once the distinction is clear, it is obvious which figures can change and which cannot — and predisposition can be separated from snapshot in the consultation. No value is a diagnosis.

concepts.title: The genes — the blueprint
concepts.text: The genes are the body’s blueprint: they set out how it uses fat and how it transports vitamin D. Small deviations in it are called gene variants, or SNPs — every person carries thousands of them, neither good nor bad. In Germany, genetic analyses fall under the Genetic Diagnostics Act (Gendiagnostikgesetz, GenDG) — information and written consent must be in place before the sample is taken.
concepts.key: The blueprint never changes. A genetic analysis is carried out once in a lifetime; a second measurement would return exactly the same result.

concepts.title: Methylation — the volume controls
concepts.text: The blueprint says nothing about what is being built right now. That is governed by chemical markers sitting on the DNA, which turn individual genes up or down; this system is known as methylation. It responds to diet, exercise, sleep and stress.
concepts.key: These values change. They do not show which genes someone has, but how active those genes currently are — which is what makes them suitable for monitoring progress.

concepts.title: MicroRNAs — the messengers in the blood
concepts.text: MicroRNAs are tiny molecules that circulate in the blood and fine-tune gene activity — short messages the body sends out continuously. Their quantity shifts faster than methylation, often within weeks.
concepts.key: Their names always follow the same pattern: "miR" plus a number. The number is simply a catalogue number and says nothing about importance.

concepts.title: Telomeres — the protective caps
concepts.text: At the ends of the chromosomes sit protective caps, much like the plastic tips on shoelaces. These telomeres keep genetic information from being lost when a cell divides — and grow a little shorter with every division.
concepts.key: Telomeres cannot be deliberately lengthened. The only thing open to influence is how quickly they shorten.

scales.v: The most common format. Red on the left, green on the right; higher is always better: 1–3 red, 4–6 yellow, 7–9 green.
The value in comparison with a reference group. 100 % means: precisely within the expected range.
A “biological age” calculated from measured values, against chronological age — a calculation, not a determination of age.

mini.caption: The miniature
mini.title: The report in miniature.
mini.lead: This miniature shows in advance which result formats this report uses. It is calculated from the sample values on this page and is not a picture. Each mark stands for a format that reappears at full size further down — and whatever this panel does not use is missing here as well.
mini.alt: Schematic miniature of the report with numbered marks for the result formats of this panel.

traffic.title: The traffic light 1–9
traffic.text: Every evaluation sits as a mark on the same traffic light 1–9. Red on the left, green on the right, higher is more favourable. How the marks spread across the band shows directly whether this panel sits more towards the red, amber or green range.

percent.title: Per cent of the reference
percent.text: The markers are given as a percentage of a matched reference group. 100 % is the normal range, higher is more favourable. The marks on the band show where the values of this sample report sit against the reference.

age.title: Biological against chronological
age.text: The dashed line is the calendar age, the dot the biological age for each marker. The distance between the two is what the report states — not the single figure in years.

trend.title: The trend as a check on progress
trend.text: Two measurements of the same value side by side: the open dot is the first, the filled one the second. Only what can actually change is compared — genetic variants stay the same. The interval between two measurements is set by the supervising institution.

consult.caption: How this becomes a consultation
consult.title: A report is a programme, not a single value.

before.title: Before the consultation
before.text: The full report is available ahead of the appointment. Read it through and mark what stands out: the traffic-light ratings, their distribution across the evaluations, the starting points named. That way it is clear from the outset what to discuss.

during.title: During the consultation
during.general: Genetic variants are determined once in a lifetime and describe the starting position. Only the epigenetic level responds to nutrition, exercise, sleep and strain — it alone is suitable for tracking progress.
during.metabolic-health: Four values in this panel sit on the epigenetic level and can therefore be influenced. The genetic variants alongside them are determined once in a lifetime and remain unchanged; they describe the starting position. Only the epigenetic level responds to nutrition, exercise, sleep and strain — it alone is suitable for tracking progress.
during.healthy-aging: All four values in this panel sit on the epigenetic level. Unlike genetic variants, which are determined once in a lifetime and remain unchanged, this level responds to nutrition, exercise, sleep and strain — it alone is suitable for tracking progress. The conversation therefore separates what is fixed from what can be worked on.
during.biologische-altersuhr: All three values in this panel sit on the epigenetic level. Unlike genetic variants, which are determined once in a lifetime and remain unchanged, this level responds to nutrition, exercise, sleep and strain — it alone is suitable for tracking progress. The conversation therefore separates what is fixed from what can be worked on.
during.telomer-analyse: This panel carries exactly one value on the epigenetic level. Unlike genetic variants, which are determined once in a lifetime and remain unchanged, it responds to nutrition, exercise, sleep and strain — it alone is suitable for tracking progress. The conversation therefore separates what is fixed from what can be worked on.
during.stress-monitor: All six values in this panel sit on the epigenetic level. Unlike genetic variants, which are determined once in a lifetime and remain unchanged, this level responds to nutrition, exercise, sleep and strain — it alone is suitable for tracking progress. The conversation therefore separates what is fixed from what can be worked on.
during.healthy-sport: Eight values in this panel sit on the epigenetic level and can therefore be influenced. The genetic variants alongside them are determined once in a lifetime and remain unchanged — they describe the starting position, not a goal. Only the epigenetic level responds to nutrition, exercise, sleep and strain; it alone is suitable for tracking progress.

after.title: Afterwards
after.general: The interval to a follow-up measurement is set by the supervising institution. Laboratory, sample material and sampling should stay the same — and whatever happens in between belongs in the same documentation as the values.
after.methylation: A follow-up measurement is meaningful at the earliest after four to six months; before that, changes cannot be measured reliably. The interval is set by the supervising institution. For comparability, the laboratory, sample material and sampling should stay the same — and whatever happens between the measurements belongs in the same documentation as the values.
